statement: The opening of Surah al-Muddaththir commands him to arise and warn, magnify his Lord, purify his garments, shun defilement, not give seeking more, and be patient.
notes: English rendering is a paraphrase of meaning.

statement: After these verses revelation came strongly and continuously.
Al-Harith ibn Hisham asked how revelation came: like the ringing of a bell (the hardest), or the angel in the form of a man. Aishah saw his forehead sweating on a very cold day.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the dataset text of Bukhari 2.

statement: Ibn Abbas: he used to move his lips with the revelation; after 75:16-19 he would listen, and recite it after Jibril left as Jibril had recited it.
notes: 'Afraid that he might lose them' follows the explanation in the narration; reviewer to confirm wording.

statement: Qur'an 73:1-5 commands the night prayer and measured recitation, and speaks of a weighty word.
notes: Paraphrase of meaning. That Surah al-Muzzammil is among the early revelations is the common view.

statement: The call was private for about three years, beginning with those closest to him.
alternatives: The length of the private phase is given variously; three years is the common report.

statement: The early believers went out to the ravines of Makkah to pray in secret.
The believers gathered in the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam near Safa, where he taught them.
notes: When the house of al-Arqam began to be used is reported differently (some place it after the call became public).

statement: Amr ibn Abasah came to him in Makkah while he was in hiding; the exchange 'What are you? A prophet... sent to join ties of kinship, break the idols, and that Allah alone be worshipped'.
notes: Direct speech. Content found in the Sahih Muslim dataset by text search (dataset no. 1930). Abd al-Baqi number 832 is from memory.
